Outliers & distances

Inspect

Outlier scores

These scores use paragraph text, as the Golf clusters do.

Score definition & corpus

Higher scores indicate greater external distance relative to within-page variation. Golf’s score formula uses the same selected text as the matrix and within-group trees.

Pages and references require ≥60 words and ≥20 per line half. References exclude the focal bifolium. Zero-denominator ratios are omitted. A selected supported page appears below the top 12 when needed.

These descriptive ratios are not significance tests. A small denominator can inflate a score.

Internal variation and nearest neighbors

The Y axis compares alternating line halves within each page. Select a point to see its nearest pages.

Read this plot

Higher points have more divergent line halves. Points farther right have a more distant second-nearest neighbor. Both axes show JS in bits.

All pages remain included, with small samples shown as hollow points. Internal JS reflects both sampling noise and differences between lines. Shorter pages tend to have higher internal JS.

References exclude the selected bifolium, but may share a bifolium with each other. Highlighted neighbors remain at their own chart coordinates, so proximity on this plot is not pairwise JS distance. Click empty space to clear the selection.

Isolation at equal word counts

How this ranking works

Ranges span percentiles from random words and contiguous text windows of the same word count. Ranking uses the lower of the two values. Equal values share a rank. The comparison group supplies the samples, while neighbors are searched across the selected text corpus.

The distance is measured to the second-closest external bifolium. Two nearby pages on the same bifolium count as one neighbor, so a single close pair cannot hide isolation. Each trial excludes both the sampled source bifolium and the selected page’s bifolium. Longer source pages contribute 32 or 64 samples per bifolium and method. Bifolia receive equal weight.

At least five source bifolia are required for a rank. Limited comparisons are shown below ranked pages. Missing results mean no estimate is available. These exploratory percentiles are not significance tests, and low scores can miss real outliers in sparse text.

Methods, sampling & data

Distances & samples

Off-diagonal cells compare full page profiles. The gold diagonal compares alternating text lines within a page. It describes sampling and heterogeneity and is excluded from clustering.

Profiles count within-word transitions in Zattera units, including start/end markers. Each context needs at least three observations on both pages. Missing contexts are not reweighted. Colors show JS divergence in bits. Trees use √JS.

The selected corpus retains every page or panel with included words. Paragraph text uses P-coded loci. All text adds C/R loci. Labels and label-only pages are excluded. Orange italic names indicate fewer than 60 words or fewer than 20 in either line half. Sparse pages can appear artificially close. Source category counts use transcription codes in metadata.

Classifications

RZ codes use René Zandbergen’s marker rules, from the 2026-10-04 snapshot. The +/− q-frequency modifiers are merged for grouping. Metadata retains the full codes.

Orders & gaps

Golf and RZ classifications are fixed. Ward linkage and optimal leaf ordering are fitted separately within each group. Golf 3a and 3b remain separate display blocks within regime 3.

Ward on this pair-dependent, context-weighted distance is exploratory and not exactly Euclidean. Its exact minimum-variance interpretation does not apply.

Physical order groups pages by quire and sheet position, then manuscript order within each bifolium. Section gaps follow transitions without moving pages. A gap can split a bifolium visually. The overview starts in manuscript order. Its menu groups pages by classification and places gaps between those groups. Pages retain manuscript order within each group. A page with multiple hands stays in a separate mixed-hand group.

Branch depth 0 leaves trees unsplit. Depth 1 shows the root split. Larger depths subdivide each tree. Separators mark hierarchy positions, not evidence for regimes or languages. Class and section gaps are twice the selected gap width.

Exports

Matrix CSV uses manuscript order with the split-half diagonal. JSON retains a zero-diagonal pairwise matrix, the separate split-half diagonal, and trees. SVG contains the current order, gaps and values.
